task_title: Review an unsafe production DB migration
output:
REQUEST CHANGES — unsafe on live heartbeat_runs (~40M, hot writes).

(1) Locks: full-table UPDATE holds long RowExclusiveLock and floods WAL/IO, so heartbeat INSERTs queue and stall. Non-CONCURRENT CREATE INDEX takes ShareLock and blocks all writes until build ends — no new heartbeat_runs rows. ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 is brief AccessExclusiveLock (PG11+ constant-default metadata); still separate it from heavy work.

(2) Single-TX backfill: one UPDATE of 40M rows = one mega-transaction (huge WAL, bloat, long snapshot, all-or-nothing rollback) that pins write pain for the entire duration and downs the heartbeat path.

(3) Safe rewrite: ADD cost_cents integer NULL; COMMIT. Batched PK-range UPDATEs, commit each batch, throttle. App dual-writes new rows. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on cost_cents. Then short ALTER SET DEFAULT 0 / SET NOT NULL when NULL=0. Never one migration TX for backfill+index; never plain CREATE INDEX here.

Artifact: /Users/glad0s/.paperclip/instances/default/companies/e212ce50-b524-408c-b3d4-0c6108d8c2e2/work-products/TSBC-1585/migration-0042-review.txt

judgeDetail.rationale: Correctly nails all three hazards (long-TX UPDATE, non-concurrent index write-blocking build, cheap PG11+ constant-default ADD COLUMN) and a concrete batched/CONCURRENTLY/SET NOT NULL rewrite, though it names ShareLock/RowExclusiveLock (accurate) but omits the cleaner NOT VALID/VALIDATE constraint path.
